production_facility.name: production_facility
production_facility.description: A production facility refers to the main area where manufacturing, processing, or assembly operations take place. In HSE, this location is associated with observations of machinery hazards, process safety, worker exposure to chemicals, and operational incidents. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe work practices, or environmental releases within the production area.
examples: Oil spill detected near the mixing station in the production facility.
Guard missing on conveyor belt in the main plant floor.
Worker reported excessive noise exposure in the assembly area.
Unlabeled chemical container found in the manufacturing hall.
Slip hazard due to coolant leak on the production line.

office_space.name: office_space
office_space.description: Office space refers to administrative or clerical work areas within an industrial site, such as rooms with desks, computers, and meeting areas. HSE observations here often involve ergonomic risks, fire safety, indoor air quality, and slips, trips, or falls. Incidents may include blocked emergency exits, poor lighting, or electrical hazards.
examples: Loose carpet tile caused a trip hazard in the main office corridor.
Blocked fire extinguisher found in the admin office.
Employee reported eye strain due to poor lighting at workstation.
Overloaded power strip observed under desk in office space.
Unattended coffee spill in the meeting room.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: A warehouse is a storage area for raw materials, finished goods, or equipment, often involving racking systems, forklifts, and loading activities. HSE concerns include manual handling injuries, falling objects, vehicle-pedestrian interactions, and fire risks. Observations may relate to blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Pallets stacked above safe height in the warehouse.
Forklift operating without horn in storage area.
Blocked emergency exit in the stockroom.
Spilled oil near loading zone in the warehouse.
Damaged racking observed in inventory area.

outdoor_area.name: outdoor_area
outdoor_area.description: Outdoor area refers to any external space on the industrial site, such as yards, parking lots, walkways, or open storage zones. HSE observations here often involve weather-related hazards, vehicle movement, environmental spills, and slips or trips. Events may include icy walkways, poor lighting, or unsecured materials exposed to wind.
examples: Icy conditions reported on the main walkway outside.
Unsecured gas cylinders found in the yard.
Oil spill observed near the parking lot entrance.
Trip hazard due to uneven pavement in outdoor area.
Poor lighting in external storage zone.

electrical_room.name: electrical_room
electrical_room.description: An electrical room is a dedicated space housing electrical panels, switchgear, transformers, or control cabinets. HSE risks include electrical shock, arc flash, fire hazards, and restricted access. Observations may involve exposed wiring, blocked access to panels, or improper use of personal protective equipment.
examples: Access to electrical room blocked by storage boxes.
Exposed live wires found in the switchgear room.
No arc flash signage on electrical panel door.
Improper PPE used during maintenance in power room.
Fire extinguisher missing from electrical enclosure.

substation.name: substation
substation.description: A substation is a facility or area where electrical voltage is transformed and distributed, often containing high-voltage equipment and transformers. HSE concerns include electrical hazards, unauthorized access, fire risk, and environmental contamination from oil-filled equipment. Observations may relate to damaged fencing, oil leaks, or missing warning signs.
examples: Oil leak detected under transformer in substation.
Unauthorized personnel found inside substation compound.
Damaged fence observed around electrical substation.
Missing high-voltage warning sign at substation gate.
Fire extinguisher not accessible in transformer yard.

workshop.name: workshop
workshop.description: A workshop is an area designated for equipment repair, fabrication, or maintenance activities, often involving tools, machinery, and manual work. HSE issues include hand injuries, machine guarding, housekeeping, and chemical exposure. Observations may include improper tool storage, lack of PPE, or spills of lubricants.
examples: Oil spill on floor in the maintenance workshop.
Bench grinder missing safety guard in repair area.
Tools left scattered on workbench in fabrication shop.
Employee not wearing gloves during equipment repair.
Improper storage of flammable liquids in tool room.

control_room.name: control_room
control_room.description: A control room is a centralized area where operators monitor and manage plant processes, often using computer systems and control panels. HSE concerns include ergonomic risks, fire safety, emergency response readiness, and access control. Observations may involve blocked egress routes, poor lighting, or malfunctioning alarm systems.
examples: Emergency exit blocked in the control room.
Operator reported faulty alarm panel in monitoring room.
Trip hazard due to loose cables in control center.
Fire extinguisher missing from process control room.
Ergonomic assessment requested for operator workstation.

corridor.name: corridor
corridor.description: A corridor is a passageway or hallway connecting different areas within a facility, used for movement of personnel and sometimes equipment. HSE observations focus on slips, trips, falls, emergency egress, and obstruction hazards. Incidents may include wet floors, blocked pathways, or poor lighting.
examples: Wet floor sign missing after cleaning in corridor.
Fire exit route blocked by boxes in hallway.
Poor lighting reported in main passageway.
Trip hazard due to loose cable in access corridor.
Spill observed in connecting corridor near office area.

loading_dock.name: loading_dock
loading_dock.description: A loading dock is a designated area for loading and unloading goods, often involving trucks, forklifts, and pallet jacks. HSE risks include vehicle-pedestrian collisions, falls from height, manual handling injuries, and pinch points. Observations may relate to unsecured dock plates, poor housekeeping, or lack of traffic controls.
examples: Dock plate not secured during unloading at loading dock.
Pedestrian walkway not marked in shipping dock area.
Pallets blocking emergency exit in loading bay.
Forklift reversing without spotter at receiving dock.
Spill of hydraulic fluid on dock platform.
